title: Amanpour’s CNN Exit Leaves Staffers Worried About Who’s Next
author: Justin Baragona
content:
Good evening, and welcome to this week's **' Ragebait.'**

**Justin Baragona** here. In tonight's edition, we take a look at what CNN
legend Christiane Amanpour's departure means for the David Ellison-owned
network, and whether others could soon follow in her footsteps. Also, I've got
news on whether CBS News will punish Bari Weiss-favorite Jan Crawford for
violating its standards and practices. Plus, what did - or didn't - the top
editorial boards and Sunday news shows say about the Ilhan Omar raid?

Announcing her pending exit from the network she's called home for the past 43
years, CNN legend **Christiane Amanpour** made no mention of **David Ellison**
and his recent [takeover](https://apnews.com/article/cnn-cbs-skydance-merger-
david-ellison-a0b39dd71b3fa6361058357835b2b76e) of the cable news giant.

"From my very first big exciting assignment covering the First Gulf War, to
the horrors of the Bosnian War, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukraine and Iran and all
the points in between, it's the teams and the camaraderie that counted so
much, as we together battled to seek the facts, the evidence and the humanity,
so that CNN could always broadcast the truth about the world and to the world,
without fear nor favor," Amanpour said in a statement this week.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

"I will be continuing my successful podcast the 'Ex-Files with Global' and
look forward to interesting new projects down the line, and will always be
rooting for CNN and maintaining its history of independent journalism," she
concluded. "Remember: always be truthful, not neutral."

While Amanpour didn't bring up the[ pro-Israel nepo media
tycoon](https://zeteo.com/p/is-this-failed-actor-nepo-baby-now) or the massive
Skydance merger in her note on her departure, which takes full effect in June,
she didn't need to. Others at the network, caught off guard by the sudden news
that one of CNN's vanguards was hanging it up, were more than willing to fill
in the blanks.
